chunks: And from him, from al-Zayyat, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).
Regarding a man who entered with a woman, he said: 'When the circumcised parts meet, the dowry becomes obligatory and the waiting period [begins].'.

key_terms.الْخِتَانَانِ: The circumcised parts (penis and vagina), indicating physical consummation
key_terms.الْعِدَّةُ: The waiting period a woman must observe after divorce or death of husband
key_terms.الْمَهْرُ: The dowry or bridal gift given to the wife

ai.seo_question: What constitutes consummation of marriage in Shia fiqh regarding dowry and iddah?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific juristic definition of consummation (tamam al-nikah) as the physical meeting of the circumcised parts, a criterion widely accepted in Shia fiqh for determining financial and temporal obligations. It establishes that upon this event, the wife becomes entitled to the full dowry (mahr) and enters the waiting period (iddah), distinguishing this state from mere contract validity. This ruling is pivotal in resolving disputes regarding partial dowries and the start of the iddah countdown in cases of separation or death.
